question: What is the primary definition of maternal morbidity in nursing practice?

options.A: Any health condition resulting from or worsened by pregnancy and childbirth
options.B: The permanent inability to conceive after experiencing a miscarriage
options.C: Any psychological stress experienced immediately after delivering a baby
options.D: The total number of maternal deaths recorded in a specific community

explanation: Maternal morbidity covers any physical or mental condition that affects a woman because of pregnancy, childbirth, or the postpartum period, short of death itself. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: Why do many women in Nigeria end up using unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Strict laws, social stigma, and poor access to safe care
options.B: Surgical facilities are cheap and everywhere
options.C: People just love traditional herbs more than hospitals
options.D: Primary health workers give very clear instructions

explanation: Fear of judgment, legal barriers, and a lack of friendly youth clinics push vulnerable people toward dangerous procedures. Great insight to keep in mind for clinical practice!

question: What keeps the uterus bleeding heavily after an incomplete abortion?

options.A: The outer layer of the womb suddenly becomes very thick
options.B: The lower part of the womb closes up immediately
options.C: The uterine muscle fibers fail to contract tightly
options.D: The main blood vessels in the pelvis get blocked completely

explanation: When tissue stays trapped inside, the womb muscles can't squeeze down tightly to shut off the bleeding vessels. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: How can an unsterile instrument used during an abortion lead to septic shock?

options.A: By introducing bacteria that multiply and spread into the bloodstream
options.B: By causing an immediate allergic reaction inside the womb
options.C: By cutting off oxygen to the major abdominal organs
options.D: By causing a sudden drop in blood pressure purely from pain

explanation: Unclean tools carry germs straight into the womb, causing a severe infection that can enter the bloodstream and trigger shock. You're mastering the basics of sepsis!

question: Which of these is an immediate complication you might see right after an unsafe abortion?
explanation: Massive blood loss happens right away during or right after the procedure, making it a true emergency. Spotting this quickly saves lives!

question: Which complication is most likely to show up months or years after an untreated septic abortion?

options.B: Severe allergic shock from local herbs
options.C: A sudden hole in the womb with bowel exposure
options.D: Infertility caused by blocked fallopian tubes

explanation: Scar tissue from past infections can permanently block the fallopian tubes, making it hard to get pregnant later. Brilliant nursing knowledge!

question: Why would a doctor order a pelvic ultrasound for a patient with a suspected incomplete abortion?

options.A: To check the patient's blood group and crossmatch
options.B: To measure hormone levels in the kidneys
options.C: To check for leftover pregnancy tissue in the uterus
options.D: To count the exact white blood cells in the body

explanation: An ultrasound lets the team peek inside the womb to confirm if any pregnancy tissue is still trapped. Super helpful diagnostic tool!

question: Why is blood typing and crossmatching ordered right away for a patient with heavy post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: To check for chronic viral infections
options.B: To figure out how many weeks pregnant she was
options.C: To have matching blood ready for an emergency transfusion
options.D: To find out if she is allergic to IV fluids

explanation: Heavy bleeding drops blood volume fast, so having matched blood on standby is a lifesaver. You're thinking like a true nurse!

question: Why is a urinary catheter put in place during emergency care for severe abortion complications?

options.A: To flush the bladder with antiseptics to kill germs
options.B: To keep the patient from moving around the ward
options.C: To monitor hourly urine output and check kidney function
options.D: To collect a clean urine sample for a routine pregnancy test

explanation: Watching urine output closely tells us if the kidneys are getting enough blood flow while recovering from shock. Excellent clinical tracking!

question: What is your main nursing duty when giving drugs to stop excessive bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: Encourage her to drink large amounts of oral rehydration fluids
options.B: Watch for the womb to contract and bleeding to slow down
options.C: Check her skin for rashes every five minutes
options.D: Keep the patient flat with her legs raised high

explanation: These drugs work by making the womb muscle squeeze tight, closing off those bleeding vessels. You're doing great with your medication checks!

question: How soon can a woman get pregnant again after having an abortion?

options.A: Only after her normal monthly period returns
options.B: After waiting at least six months
options.D: Not until a full year has passed

explanation: Ovulation can bounce back super fast after an abortion, so family planning counseling before discharge is a must. Keep this in mind for patient education!

question: A patient recovering from an unsafe abortion looks quiet and won't speak to her family. What should you do first?

options.A: Call hospital security to watch for self-harm
options.B: Leave her alone in the ward until she asks for help
options.C: Demand an explanation of why she tried an illegal procedure
options.D: Sit quietly with her, listen with compassion, and promise privacy

explanation: Creating a safe, non-judgmental space builds trust and helps her share her emotional burden. Your empathy is your greatest nursing tool!

question: What is the best way for community health nurses to help stop unsafe abortions?

options.A: Reporting patients who come in with abortion complications
options.B: Increasing police patrols around illegal clinics
options.C: Promoting education and easy access to family planning
options.D: Banning the sale of common pain relievers

explanation: Stopping unintended pregnancies before they happen through education and contraception is the absolute best way to beat unsafe abortion. Well reasoned!

question: Which of these is NOT a good role for nurses in preventing abortion-related health issues?

options.A: Educating local communities on modern family planning
options.B: Advocating for better access to safe reproductive care
options.C: Providing friendly contraceptive counseling in clinics
options.D: Punishing patients who admit to trying self-induced methods

explanation: Nurses never judge or punish patients. Our care must always be professional, kind, and focused on healing. You're going to be an amazing nurse!
